questions.question: What should you do if you must ride on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, reduce your speed. Avoid sudden moves. Use both brakes carefully.

questions.question: Why should you avoid riding directly next to another vehicle?

options.text: The driver may want to pass you in your lane.
You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
You will have access to escape routes.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding next to another vehicle is dangerous. The driver may not see you in their blind spot. The vehicle could also block your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: What is the safest part of the lane?
questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always safest. Change your position based on the situation around you.

questions.question: Do motorcycle mirrors have blind spots?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, just like car mirrors
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, just like car mirrors. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do if a vehicle is tailgating you?

options.text: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to let them pass or slow down to create more space ahead
questions.explanation: Encourage the tailgater to pass. Speeding up only makes them tailgate faster, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes
Turn around and find another route

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing with flashing lights, you must stop completely. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before going. Never try to go around a train.

questions.question: What should you do after riding over an object on the road?

options.text: Keep riding because the danger is over
Pull to the side and check your tires and rims for damage
Stop to remove the object from the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side and check your tires and rims for damage
questions.explanation: Pull off the road to check for tire and rim damage. Also check that nothing is caught in the chain or belt before riding again.

questions.question: You see a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights. What should you do?

options.text: Stop on the road behind the emergency vehicle
Wait until the emergency vehicle starts moving
Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes away from the emergency vehicle
questions.explanation: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle. Slow down and be ready to stop. Give the emergency vehicle extra space.

questions.question: Can one alcoholic drink affect your ability to ride?

options.text: No, one drink will not lead to a DUI conviction
No, one drink will never affect your riding
Yes, one drink can affect your riding ability

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, one drink can affect your riding ability
questions.explanation: Impairment starts with the first drink. You can be convicted of riding impaired even below the legal blood alcohol limit.

questions.question: When riding in the left third of a lane, the driver can see you in their side mirror. What is the problem with this?

options.text: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror
Wind can prevent the use of a side mirror
Drivers should not use side mirrors

questions.correctAnswerText: Most drivers don't check their side mirrors as often as their rearview mirror
questions.explanation: Drivers check their rearview mirror more often than side mirrors. It is safer to ride in the center of the lane where the driver is more likely to see you.

questions.question: Pick a lane position that:

options.text: Makes you visible to others and keeps safe space around you.
You like, without thinking about other riders.
Gets you close to other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes you visible to others and keeps safe space around you.
questions.explanation: Choose a spot in your lane where other drivers can see you easily. Keep space around your motorcycle. No single lane position works best all the time. Good riders change positions as conditions change.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. You should:

options.text: Not wear bright clothing during the day.
Wear bright clothing during the day.
Wear dark clothing during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing during the day.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Wear bright clothing when you ride, even during the day. This makes you easier to see.

questions.question: Riding is harder when rain just starts because:

options.text: Other drivers may not react quickly to rain.
Other drivers do not drive fast enough.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement becomes very slippery.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the pavement is very slippery. Oil from vehicles has not yet washed away. It mixes with water to create a slick surface.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow-moving vehicle
questions.explanation: This sign is on the back of slow vehicles moving below 25 mph, like farm equipment or construction vehicles.

questions.question: What is most important when buying a motorcycle helmet?
questions.correctAnswerText: Protection
questions.explanation: Protection matters most when buying a helmet. Get one that fastens securely, fits properly, and is DOT-approved.

questions.question: When riding at night, it is:

options.text: Easier to judge distances than during the day.
About as easy to judge distances as during the day.
Harder to judge distances than during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Harder to judge distances than during the day.
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances at night than during the day. Shadows and light help you see distance. At night, artificial lights distort these clues or remove them completely.

questions.question: What is the best footwear for motorcycle riders?
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather boots
questions.explanation: Leather boots give the most protection. They should be tall and strong enough to cover and support your ankles.

questions.question: Riding gloves should be made of:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather.
questions.explanation: Riding gloves should be leather or similar tough material. This gives you the best grip and protection.

questions.question: Motorcycles have blind spots. Riders should:

options.text: Ignore them if the motorcycle has a mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always check them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic before changing lanes. Make this a routine habit.

questions.question: Long-term exposure to wind noise:
questions.correctAnswerText: Can permanently damage your hearing.
questions.explanation: Long-term wind noise can cause permanent hearing loss. Wear ear protection while riding. Good ear protection lets you hear important sounds like sirens and car horns.

questions.question: When riding during the day, you should:

options.text: Wear dark clothes because it is light outside.
Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
Wear comfortable clothes like shorts if it is hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothes so other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors when riding so other drivers can see you better.

questions.question: To reduce your chances of a crash, you should:

options.text: Use the correct position in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the correct position in your lane.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to others, use turn signals, keep safe distance from other vehicles, look ahead 12 seconds, spot hazards early, and be ready to react to changes.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping a motorcycle, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears using the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear when stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: When stopping, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes.
questions.explanation: Use both the front and rear brakes every time you slow or stop.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should:

options.text: Check that your brake lights work.
Check that the paint is not peeling.
Make sure your bike is completely clean.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that your brake lights work.
questions.explanation: Before every ride, do safety checks. Test your front and rear brakes to make sure each one turns on the brake lights.
